pattern.shared_shape: Both non-right heads leave awarded lots outside S on results the store did not key to a lot (lot = null), and both are vouched by a notice-level TED-VAL_TOTAL whose coverage R10 never compares with the summed lots.
pattern.6465510: wrong/other: 20 award notices, 19 of them single-Lot-section F03s whose results are stored lot = null and awarded = null; S sums the 2 keyed lots (LOT-2, LOT-6), about 19 % of the ~EUR 860k awarded. The vouch, 20772908 VAL_TOTAL EUR 161,290.32, is the single-lot award notice of printed lot 4 (= lot 4's CN VAL_OBJECT), a lot not in S, 0.45 % from S by coincidence. R10's 'not a single-lot notice's own award' exclusion is evaluated on the stored award row, which is null here, so it lets the figure through.
pattern.7749755: neutral/other: S sums lots 1, 6, 9 of award notice 23353167 and is vouched by that same notice's VAL_TOTAL (an identity, not a procedure total); lots 2 and 5 were awarded in single-lot F03s whose LotResult prints no LOT_NO, so they sit lot = null; S covers 49.85 % of the EUR 8,274.00 awarded, the head without W 39.0 %.
pattern.same_family_rights: 6779279 (S/truth 95.4 %), 6850401 (90.1 %), 7698260 (81.2 %): the read18 note-2 partial-sum shape, right only because the head without W holds the single left-out lot.
guards_R1_R10_miss: G-cover: an award-type vouching total (TED-VAL_TOTAL, BT-161, BT-118, BT-1118, TED-LOW/HIGH) must come from a notice that awards at least one summed key. On the 61 served snapshots it refuses exactly 6465510 and no right (the vouching notice awards none of LOT-2/LOT-6). Equivalent here: judge R10's single-lot exclusion by the notice's own structure (one Lot section / one LotResult), not by whether its award row was stored with a value.

G-unplaced (measurement, not proposed as a refusal): an award on a lot = null result that restates no summed award. It marks exactly the partial-sum family (6779279, 6850401, 7698260, 7749755) and refusing on it would cost 3 rights for 1 neutral. The fix for that family is placement (key a single-Lot-section notice's LotResult by its sole Lot section's LOT_NO, the 567/570 follow-on) plus R10 accepting the sum of disjoint notice totals (read18 note 2); with both, all four become full sums vouched by their notices' totals.

(1) Each summed lot is real and appears once. CAN 21253579 prints LotResult RES-1 to RES-4 with LOT_NO 1, 4, 6, 7 and CONTRACT_NO 1, 4, 6, 7. (2) The vouch is genuine. It is the CAN's procedure-level VAL_TOTAL with type PROCUREMENT_TOTAL, an award total rather than an estimate that S merely happens to match. It covers only the four lots awarded in that notice, though, not the whole procedure.

LOT_NO 2 is office-equipment consumables (консумативи за офис техника), awarded on 2021-09-23 in CAN 21988563 to Кооперация ПАНДА for BGN 324,400, with 6 tenders. Each CAN covers one lot, and its notice-scope VAL_TOTAL equals only that lot's award, so the CANs are not cumulative and summing them counts nothing twice. S = 591,400 is the real sum of two additive awards, each with its own single supplier; no ceiling is shared across lots. The vouch is this procedure's own estimated total. S equals it because each award equals its lot estimate (the usual Bulgarian practice of awarding at the budgeted value). The estimate does not belong to some other object. There is no slip and no VAT mix. S is the procedure's true award total and clearly beats the one-lot head of 324,400.

skeptic.why:
I re-fetched the tender and all three notices (files under read/sk6993571_*) and tried to refute the reader. I could not.
(1) The two lots are distinct. CN 21506205 prints LOT_NO 1 "Доставка на канцеларски материали…" (VAL_OBJECT 267,000) and LOT_NO 2 "Доставка на консумативи за офис техника…" (VAL_OBJECT 324,400). CAN 21852608 has a single LotResult for LOT_NO 1: contract 4070 of 2021-07-19, Ай Ес Джей Груп ЕООД (national id 200011753), 8 tenders, VAL_TOTAL 267,000. CAN 21988563 has a single LotResult for LOT_NO 2: contract 15630 of 2021-09-23, Кооперация ПАНДА (000885099), 6 tenders, VAL_TOTAL 324,400. Each CAN's INFO_ADD names its own lot (Обособена позиция 1 / № 2). Different contract numbers, winners and dates. The versions list holds only CN, CAN1 and CAN2, so there is no re-award.
One keying hazard: CAN 21988563's lot section has section_id LOT-1 while its LOT_NO is 2. The snapshot keys it correctly as LOT-2, so lot 1 is not counted twice.
(2) It is additive, not a shared framework. The CN says each lot's estimate is "максимално допустимата стойност на договора" (2-year call-off up to that ceiling). Each ceiling belongs to one lot and one supplier under a separate contract, so the two ceilings add. That is why each award equals its lot estimate exactly. It is not a coincidence.
(3) The vouch is not an estimate S merely matches. The CN's INFO_ADD shows 591,400 is exactly this procedure's residual value (lots 1+2, без ДДС). Lots 3–7 (403.64 + 1,828.52 + 5,133.10 + 4,166.67 + 29,166.67 BGN) were split off for direct award and are not in this Tender.
(4) There is no x10^k slip: 267,000 + 324,400 = 591,400 matches the CN to the cent. Everything is on a net (excl. VAT) basis. The CN says без ДДС, and the performance guarantee is computed on the прогнозна стойност без ДДС.
S = 591,400 BGN is the real total of the two awarded contracts. The head without path W serves 324,400, which is lot 2 alone and misses 45% of the procedure. S is clearly better.
One caveat: both awards are ceilings, so actual spend may be lower. The same is true of the head's figure, so it does not change the ranking.
